 Get UNHCR to cover refugees’ hospital bills, says Radzi
 17-Nov-2026, 18:34 17 Nov 2026, 18:34 Anne Muhammad Share The Putrajaya MP accuses the UN agency of issuing cards to refugees indiscriminately without taking responsibility for them.
 Radzi Jidin said the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 showed that outstanding medical bills in 2025 amounted to RM336 million, of which RM281 million was owed by non-citizens. 
 PETALING JAYA : Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) has urged the government to make the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) responsible for paying the hospital bills of cardholding refugees. 
 Speaking in the Dewan Rakyat today, he cited a ministerial reply on June 15 which said that most outstanding medical bills owed by foreigners involved undocumented migrants.
 He also cited deputy health minister Hanifah Hajar Taib as saying on Oct 7 that more than 80% of outstanding bills owed by non-citizen patients involved undocumented migrants or stateless individuals.
 Radzi noted that, according to the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026, outstanding medical bills in 2025 stood at RM336 million, of which RM281 million was owed by non-citizens.
 “This means there are loopholes in the system. They know they can enter and we will admit them. When they are discharged, they don’t have to pay; it’s fine, they can just leave. If we allow this to continue, we will see immense pressure on our national healthcare system,” he said.
 Radzi accused the UNHCR of issuing cards to refugees indiscriminately without taking responsibility for them.
 “Can we not put pressure on UNHCR to provide insurance for everyone to whom it issues these cards? If it is so willing to issue cards allowing refugees to enter, fine, it must take responsibility and provide insurance.
 “What will happen if we put pressure on them in this way? They will not want to spend so much money every year on providing insurance, and this will accelerate the resettlement of refugees in third countries,” he said.
 On Nov 3, Radzi questioned why UNHCR still appeared to be registering refugees despite a Cabinet directive in July to suspend registrations.
 He pointed to an image circulating on social media that appeared to show a UNHCR registration card dated Oct 29. He also said the UN agency’s online registration portal remained accessible.
 In response, deputy foreign minister Lukanisman Awang Sauni acknowledged that monitoring of UNHCR’s registration activities might not yet be sufficiently stringent.
 He said the government was still finalising its own refugee registration system, under which only about 147 refugees had been registered since January because of a staff shortage.
 Lukanisman said Malaysia was also pressing UNHCR to speed up the resettlement of refugees in third countries, although fewer countries were accepting them.
